1790-1860

Caption This

The South, Slavery, and Reform

7

How this works (15–20 minutes)

  1. Look at each of the 5 images. Read the “What you’re looking at” line.
  2. Write a short, funny caption, like a meme. Pick a caption style if you want one.
  3. Then write 2–3 sentences about what is really going on. Use at least one key term from the lesson. Type the key term in English, exactly as shown.
  4. Save Progress any time. When all 5 are done, press Finished and upload the file to Canvas.

Keep it respectful: make the joke about the politics, the decision, or the mistake. Never joke about enslaved people, anyone’s race or religion, people who struggle with alcohol, or people who were hurt.

Domestic slave trade map

Not done

What you’re looking at: Map 11.2, “Routes of the U.S. Domestic Slave Trade, 1810s through 1850s,” from your Norton textbook, Ch. 11. Green arrows show the 1810s to 1830s. Blue arrows show the 1840s to 1850s. Dots mark slave-trading hubs. This is a serious topic, so write a serious caption, not a joke.

Heads up: This one is serious. Write one clear, thoughtful line. No jokes about the people who were sold.

  • Which direction do most of the arrows point?
  • Name two cities marked with a dot.
